title: Hidden Tuition: An Insider's Guide to College Pricing and Financial Aid
description: The secret economics of maximizing college financial aid (and why it’s not as miserable as you think). In the college admissions process, a terrifying unknown looms large: How much is this really going to cost? For prospective students and their families, there’s no easy answer. While college prices continue to rise, so do their promises of financial aid for qualified students. But who qualifies? And for how much? How can this monumental life decision be so utterly impossible to understand? Hidden Tuition is an insider’s guide for navigating college financial aid to maximum effect and with (relatively) minimal pain. Economist and financial-aid expert Phillip B. Levine draws on his unique experience—including years of research in higher-education finance and work alongside admissions and financial-aid departments—to help readers first identify, then minimize, what they’ll actually pay for different types of colleges based on their circumstances. With expertise, clarity, and the warmth of someone who’s been through it, Levine details how students can find the hidden tuition costs in the opaque landscape of college pricing and financial aid. He explores topics that include: Why college’s “sticker prices” are rarely what students pay—and how some actual prices are even going down The best, worst, and most surprising deals for students with different financial resources How to navigate financial aid for divorced and multi-residence households Who really benefits from early decision How the nature of scholarships and merit-based aid is often framed in misleading ways The pros and cons of college savings accounts When and how to get started on college financing Why all student loans aren't the same (or aren't all that bad) Debunking common myths and offering practical guidance

title: Europe for ₹0 Tuition: The Indian Student’s Hidden Continent for World-Class Education at
description: Most Indian students believe that studying abroad means spending ₹40–80 lakh in countries like the US, UK, or Canada. That belief is incomplete. Across Europe, there are universities that offer world-class education at little to no tuition cost — in countries like Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden, Norway, France, and more. Yet, most Indian students never discover these opportunities. Europe for ₹0 Tuition is not a typical study abroad guide. It is a practical, reality-based roadmap to accessing high-quality international education without financial burden. Inside this book, you will learn: ✔ How Germany offers near-zero tuition education ✔ The real cost of studying in Europe (far lower than you think) ✔ Countries where you can study in English without learning local languages ✔ How to choose between Germany, Netherlands, Sweden, France, and others ✔ Scholarships like DAAD, Erasmus, SISGP, Eiffel explained simply ✔ The truth about living costs in European cities ✔ Student visa processes across Europe ✔ Work opportunities and PR pathways after graduation ✔ Common mistakes Indian students make while applying This book is based on real cases, real numbers, and real outcomes — not assumptions. If you are: Planning to study abroad Worried about high costs or loans Exploring alternatives to US, UK, Canada Or looking for smarter, cost-effective options Then this book gives you a clear, structured, and realistic pathway . You don’t need ₹50 lakh to study abroad. You need the right information. title: The Hidden Curriculum: First Generation Students at Legacy Universities
description: A revealing look at the experiences of first generation students on elite campuses and the hidden curriculum they must master in order to succeed College has long been viewed as an opportunity for advancement and mobility for talented students regardless of background. Yet for first generation students, elite universities can often seem like bastions of privilege, with unspoken academic norms and social rules. The Hidden Curriculum draws on more than one hundred in-depth interviews with students at Harvard and Georgetown to offer vital lessons about the challenges of being the first in the family to go to college, while also providing invaluable insights into the hurdles that all undergraduates face. As Rachel Gable follows two cohorts of first generation students and their continuing generation peers, she discovers surprising similarities as well as striking differences in their college experiences. She reveals how the hidden curriculum at legacy universities often catches first generation students off guard, and poignantly describes the disorienting encounters on campus that confound them and threaten to derail their success. Gable shows how first-gens are as varied as any other demographic group, and urges universities to make the most of the diverse perspectives and insights these talented students have to offer. The Hidden Curriculum gives essential guidance on the critical questions that university leaders need to consider as they strive to support first generation students on campus, and demonstrates how universities can balance historical legacies and elite status with practices and policies that are equitable and inclusive for all students.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_3"]', '#CardInstanceOUABfV2ZklKB8gy1ApE

title: 11 Plus Verbal Reasoning Workbook: For GL-style preparation
description: Build confidence with words, letters, numbers and logic. Four 80-question practice papers, each with an answer grid and suggested timing. Answers and concise explanations at the back to support independent review. Practise closest and opposite meanings, analogies, compound words, missing and hidden words, letter extraction, encoding and decoding, number sequences, ordering and deduction. title: Is College a Lousy Investment?: Negotiating the Hidden Costs of Higher Education
description: Is College a Lousy Investment?: Negotiating the Hidden Cost of Higher Education discusses many of the economic misconceptions about earning a college degree. While it is widely believed that attending college guarantees wealth and success, students, concerned parents, and higher education professionals have neglected calculating the full-range of short-term and long-terms costs. Our work illustrates how the promotion of education merely as a commodity come at a high price for the individual and society. title: CASH FOR COLLEGE: The Middle-Class Family’s Complete Guide to Paying Less for College
description: The average college graduate carries $39,547 in student debt. That doesn't have to be your student's story. If your family earns $80,000 to $200,000, you're caught in the middle—too wealthy for need-based aid, not wealthy enough for $70,000 sticker prices. The financial aid system isn't designed to help you. It's designed to confuse you into paying full price. This book changes that. After twenty years as a college counselor advising over 300 student-athletes from 56 countries, I've helped hundreds of families find money they didn't know existed—and choose schools that actually lead to careers, not just diplomas. Inside, you'll discover: Why 75% of families who appeal their aid packages at private colleges get more money—and the exact scripts to use when you call How to find "Hidden Ivy" schools that cost less than your state university but deliver elite career outcomes The employer pipeline research toolkit that reveals which companies are hiring from which schools—before your student applies How employer tuition programs at Starbucks, Walmart, Amazon, and Target can cover an entire degree How your student can arrive at college with a full year of credits for approximately $1,200 The funding stack strategy one family used to drop their cost from $68,000 to $21,750 per year Twenty chapters. Over fifty funding sources. Real families who made it work. Every chapter opens with a dollar value showing exactly what those strategies are worth to your family. Includes worksheets, appeal letter templates, a grade-by-grade action timeline, and twelve reference appendices. Written for the Growth Parent—the one who sees their kid, does the research, and refuses to choose between a great education and financial sanity. Same destination.
